Finnish Exports Rebound as Canadian Tariffs Lifted After Three-Month Standoff

Finnish exporters are resuming shipments to Canada this week after Ottawa lifted sweeping trade restrictions that had affected a wide range of Finnish goods for nearly three months. The measures, which included broad-based tariffs of up to 25% on sectors from machinery to paper products, were imposed in late February amid a dispute over digital service taxes and environmental standards.

The trade barriers, described by Finland’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs as “unprecedented in scope,” caused a sharp contraction in exports to Canada, which had accounted for €1.2 billion in annual Finnish trade. According to the Finnish Confederation of Industries, shipments to Canada fell by 68% in March and April, with major disruptions seen in forestry, technology, and food processing.

Negotiations between Helsinki and Ottawa intensified in May, culminating in a joint statement last Friday announcing the removal of the tariffs and a commitment to address digital taxation disputes through the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

“Restoring access to the Canadian market is vital for Finnish businesses and workers,” said Paavo Niemelä, Under-Secretary of State for External Economic Relations. “This agreement safeguards thousands of jobs and strengthens our trade ties with a key partner.”

Exporters have already begun ramping up deliveries. Markku Salonen, CEO of Lumenek Oy, a major machinery exporter, told reporters, “We are working overtime to fulfill back orders and restore trust with our Canadian partners.”

Analysts note that while the immediate impact has been mitigated, some manufacturers may face longer-term challenges regaining lost market share. “The episode has underscored the vulnerability of Finland’s open economy to external shocks,” said Riikka Koivisto, trade analyst at Nordmark Research.

Finnish customs data for June are expected to reflect a rebound, though industry groups caution that full recovery could take several months.
